title: ARES reproducible reference scenario

humanMission.habitatSelection: Flat site (under 4° within 120 m) chosen with tools/find-habitat.mjs so that the straight line to Rochette crosses steep mapped terrain.

classes.method: Quartiles of brightness within this terrain subset: cool = lowest 25%, warm = highest 25%.

surface.interpretation: Relative night-brightness quartiles within this subset, not calibrated temperature, thermal inertia or ground strength. Context for B; experimental doubled cell cost in the lowest quartile for C. No walking-safety benefit has been validated.

plausibility.description: Observed share of high-brightness cells by mapped slope band in this subset; descriptive association, not independent validation of a ground-material class.

radiation.source: Curiosity RAD, Gale crater, Aug 2012-Jun 2013; Hassler et al. (2014) Science 343, doi:10.1126/science.1244797; value as reported by SwRI

routeC.description: Terrain-aware cost multiplied by (1 + weight) on cells in the coolest night-IR quartile. Uncalibrated relative brightness; no ground-strength classification or walking-safety benefit has been validated.

limitations: Prototype terrain cost, slope threshold and walkback pace factor are assumptions, not NASA EVA policy. The habitat location is hypothetical. Orbital terrain cannot resolve every hazard. Time scenarios are what-if assumptions, not statistical confidence intervals or suit-performance predictions.
